x: Bob Coates was another to have a disappointing race but the real disaster fell on Dave De Bondi who never got near his usual form and only managed to finish after a heroic struggle.

Aussie Dave De Bondi determined to make a good showing at his first attempt. The veterans of Belgrave, well versed in the ways of the Brighton road, stand quietly out of the way of brasher newcomers with less experience and more to say;John Keown and John Morris are joined this year by John Johnson and Wally Wortley.
Australian Dave de Bondi, who had kept an eye on his clubmates during the early stages of the race, snatched a few hours sleep and drove over to Essex for a 50 kms. race on the Saturday afternoon.
Our Australian visitor Dave De Bondi has returned to his country. He is still training in the Australian hills and is hoping to get a little faster.

DAVE DE BONDI and VIC TOWNSEND both send their regards to all Bels. It is pleasing to hear (via Harry Shields) that our Past President ALF TAYLOR and his wife JENNY are both well in their Somerset retreat.

Overall a disappointing result for the Bels but a trip not to be forgotten in a hurry. Other Belgravians making an appearance were Vic Townsend who was 2nd in a veterans race and Dave De Bondi over from Australia to watch.
News from overseas indicates that Allan has settled in to his new abode and Dave De Bondi is changing status at last. He is marrying a physiotherapist who one hopes will speed Dave up.

Also news of Dave De Bondi in Australia who has now bought himself a plot of land and is progressing in his house building ambitions. John Knifton has also written (he represents the U.S.A. regularly) informing of his exploits with dogs while out training.
From the U.S.A. we had Gertz Klopfer (placed in London to Brighton Walk) and Tom Dooley and from 'down under' came two "Aussies" Dave de Bondi and Alan Lucas.
